Proof of (2). Choose a scheme <MATH_0001> and a surjective smooth morphism
<MATH_0002>. Consider the fibre product
<MATH_0003>
Recall that <MATH_0004> is the automorphism group algebraic space of
<MATH_0005>. By Groupoids in Spaces, Lemma
<REF_0001>
there is a maximal open subscheme <MATH_0006>
such that <MATH_0007> is locally quasi-finite.
Moreover, formation of <MATH_0008> commutes with arbitrary
base change. In particular the two inverse images of <MATH_0009>
in <MATH_0010> are the same open subspace of <MATH_0011>
(since after all the two maps <MATH_0012> are isomorphic
and hence have isomorphic automorphism group spaces).
Hence <MATH_0013> is the inverse image of an open substack
<MATH_0014> by
Properties of Stacks, Lemma
<REF_0002>
and we have a cartesian diagram
<MATH_0015>
Thus the morphism <MATH_0016>
is locally quasi-finite and we conclude that
<MATH_0017> is quasi-DM by Lemma <REF_0003>
part (5). On the other hand, if <MATH_0018>
is an open substack which is quasi-DM, then the inverse image
<MATH_0019> of <MATH_0020> must be contained in <MATH_0021> by our
construction of <MATH_0022> since
<MATH_0023>
is locally quasi-finite over <MATH_0024>.
Thus <MATH_0025> is the quasi-DM locus.
Finally, choose a field extension <MATH_0026> and a <MATH_0027>-commutative
diagram
<MATH_0028>
Then we find an isomorphism
<MATH_0029>
of group algebraic spaces over <MATH_0030>. Hence <MATH_0031> is locally quasi-finite
over <MATH_0032> if and only if <MATH_0033> maps into <MATH_0034>
(use the commutation of formation of <MATH_0035> and
Groupoids in Spaces, Lemma
<REF_0004>
applied to <MATH_0036> and <MATH_0037> to see this).
This finishes the proof of (2). The proof of (1) is
exactly the same.
